circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street course encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various supporting motorsport events. The track holds FIA Grade 1 certification status.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The 4. 326 km circuit in Spielberg, Austria, originally called the Österreichring, served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix from 1970 to 1987 before undergoing reconstruction and renaming. Following its redesign as the A1-Ring, it resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix for another seven-year period starting in 1997.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Located on a street course near Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, this 6. 003 km track ranks as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming a permanent fixture on the calendar with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Bahrain International Circuit, a 5. 412 km venue established in 2004, hosts the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix and holds the distinction of staging the first Middle Eastern Formula One race that year. The track accommodates various motorsport events including GP2 racing, 24-hour endurance competitions, and previously Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 to 2010, while maintaining FIA Grade 1 certification with multiple configurable layouts.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced combination of extended straights and diverse corner types, making it a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle capabilities. The venue, which holds FIA Grade 1 certification, accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated near Spa in Belgium's Wallonia region, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a mainstay of Formula One racing since 1950, when it featured in the championship's inaugural season. The track has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix consistently since 1985, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006, establishing itself as one of motorsport's most enduring venues.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that annually hosts the Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport series including sportscar championships and North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, before resuming the event from 2024 onward. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing competitions, establishing itself as a multi-category racing destination.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone has been England's premier racing venue since hosting the inaugural British Grand Prix in 1948, and gained historic significance in 1950 by staging the opening race of the World Championship of Drivers. After alternating between three tracks from the mid-1950s to mid-1980s, the British Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe in 1986. Built in just eight months starting from late 1985, it was constructed outside the city as a compromise when plans for a Monaco-style street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by the government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as one of Europe's earliest purpose-built racing venues. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 with only one interruption, it remains a Formula One calendar staple and earns its "Temple of Speed" nickname through its notably fast layout featuring extended straights and high-velocity corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Located in Mie Prefecture, Japan, Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807-kilometer track operated by Honda Mobilityland that hosts major international racing events. The facility, which can accommodate 155,000 spectators, is primarily recognized for staging Formula One and Japanese Super Formula championship races.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard with its concentration of major hotels and casinos. The track weaves through iconic locations including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of the most visually distinctive venues on the racing calendar.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two Mexican racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who both perished in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, most recently from 2015 onwards under the Mexico City Grand Prix banner, following earlier stints on a different configuration that concluded in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that measures 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, it joined the championship calendar in 2022 and hosts the Miami Grand Prix annually.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 kilometres through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, weaving around the harbour in the Principality of Monaco. Though officially named after Monaco itself, the circuit is widely known as Monte Carlo since most of its layout occupies that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the dunes near the North Sea coast in the Netherlands, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026 after a lengthy absence from Formula One. The track earns its popular nickname "The Roller coaster in the Dunes" from its dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz, which create a uniquely challenging racing experience through the coastal landscape.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Situated near Lusail in northern Qatar, this FIA Grade 1 licensed circuit stretches 5. 419 kilometers and features a notably long main straight of over one kilometer. The track is protected by surrounding artificial grass that prevents sand from drifting onto the racing surface.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km motorsport venue in São Paulo, Brazil, opened in 1940 and renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise circuit features supporting facilities including a karting track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street course positioned along Jeddah's waterfront beside the Red Sea, serving as the venue for the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in Formula One since its inaugural running in 2021.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is an urban racing venue in Singapore that winds through the Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km track features a balanced mix of extended straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the primary venue for Formula One's United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major motorsport events including MotoGP and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, while previously accommodating various other racing series such as IndyCar and rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai-British driver Alexander Albon currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 and claimed 32 race victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved significant success in endurance racing, including World Endurance Championship and multiple Le Mans victories, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One and World Sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured the 2026 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Mercedes, setting the record as sport's youngest champion. Since his 2025 debut, he has accumulated nine race victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Haas. He has established himself as a regular competitor on the Formula One grid.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One, competing for the Audi team in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his long career spanning 13 seasons. He has claimed 10 Grand Prix victories and came close to the championship title on two occasions while driving for Mercedes, finishing second in both 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One for Alpine, representing his nation in the sport's top category.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian racing driver, holds a reserve driver position with Haas in Formula One and has made seven Grand Prix appearances since 2024. He competes in endurance racing, having driven for Nielsen Racing in the European Le Mans Series and currently racing in the LMP2 category with AF Corse in the Asian Le Mans Series.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a significant achievement in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One while competing for Red Bull Racing, holding dual French and Algerian nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton, a British driver competing for Ferrari, stands among motorsport's greatest achievers with seven world championships matching Michael Schumacher's record tally. His career statistics are unparalleled, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved endurance racing success by winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, currently drives for Racing Bulls in the Formula One World Championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc is a Monégasque Formula One competitor for Ferrari who has achieved nine Grand Prix victories throughout his racing career. He came close to the world championship in 2022, finishing as runner-up in the drivers' standings while driving for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver, has competed across multiple racing series including a Formula One career spanning 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he races for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT while pursuing part-time opportunities in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Over his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French motorsport competitor, most recently raced for Haas in Formula One after previously achieving a Grand Prix victory with Alpine at the 2021 Hungarian round.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac, bringing extensive experience from a career spanning 15 seasons. He achieved his highest championship finish as runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has secured six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri competes in Formula One for McLaren, where he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories during his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his racing career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed eight race victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during the 2023-2024 seasons before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor currently driving for Aston Martin in Formula One racing.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese racing driver, held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role for Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch and Belgian racer competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Throughout his 12 seasons in Formula One, he has secured 74 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu remains the sole Chinese driver to have competed in Formula One, having raced in the sport from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based outfit has operated as Alpine's works team since 2021, when Renault rebranded its racing division to spotlight its Alpine sports car marque. Following Renault's withdrawal from the championship at the end of 2025, the team transitioned away from direct manufacturer backing after competing under the French automotive giant's control for several years.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has been involved in Formula One through multiple incarnations as a British constructor. The present operation, run by AMR GP Limited, competes under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury manufacturer Ferrari, is the sport's most decorated and longest-serving competitor, having participated continuously in every Formula One World Championship since 1950. The team is colloquially known as "the Prancing Horse" and holds the distinction of being both the oldest active and most successful outfit in the championship's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American-licensed Haas F1 is owned by NASCAR entrepreneur Gene Haas and entered Formula One competition in 2016 following its establishment in 2014. The team is currently led by principal Ayao Komatsu, who assumed leadership after Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering company established itself as an independent Formula One constructor beginning in 1993, while also achieving endurance racing success including victory at Le Mans in 1989. The team competed in Formula One through various transformations until 2025, when it was acquired by Audi AG to serve as the foundation for Audi's factory team entry into the sport.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking, operating as a subsidiary within the McLaren Group under Bahraini ownership through Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes-Benz has maintained a significant presence in Formula One since 1954 through both team ownership and engine supply, with the current operation based in Brackley competing as Mercedes-AMG Petronas and holding a German racing licence. In 2022, Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff as equal partners in the team's ownership structure. The marque's racing teams are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor established in 2024 that operates as a sister team to Red Bull Racing under Red Bull GmbH ownership. Based in Faenza with a supporting facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's second constructor entry on the grid alongside its primary racing operation.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as a sister outfit to Red Bull Racing under Austrian ownership. Operating from Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, it represents one of two constructor entities within the Red Bull GmbH motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, competing under an Austrian licence from its English base, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and became one of two championship teams operated by Red Bull GmbH, alongside Racing Bulls. Christian Horner led the team from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies taking over the leadership role in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerging from Williams's prior unsuccessful racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team banner and operates from a substantial facility spanning 60 acres.
